title: Hearing the teenage Art Tatum at the blind school in Columbus
summary: A pianist took him to a Columbus blind school to hear a 14 or 15-year-old he calls the greatest piano player in the world, who played as well with either hand.

venues.name: Ohio State School for the Blind

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Art Tatum: the legend, the piano and the man

blocks.x: Tell me the story about how you met Tatum the first time.

Oh, you want to hear that? Well, it was the band I was playing... You know, one of the first bands I ever played with was in Columbus, Ohio. It wasn't the very first one, but it was one of the first ones. And the piano player came to me one day and said, 'Man, I want you to go with me and hear the greatest piano player in the world.' So I, you know, went along with him. I didn't know where he was going, but it wound up we went to a blind school in Columbus. And he introduced me to this little skinny guy. He said, 'This is the greatest piano player in the world.' And this kid was around fifteen, fourteen or fifteen years old, you know. And he sat down at the piano, and really, he convinced me.

Yes. He played so much... He played the same thing with his left hand as he did with his right hand; you know, all that fast... He'd do it... He could play it one-handed. Didn't need two hands. Either hand, don't make
no difference. That's how I first met him.
But he was still in school then.
Yeah, he was going to blind school.
He was going to blind school. I don't know. I think he had made a couple of concert tours -- then.
He was a genius, you know.
So you heard about him...actually heard him playing much sooner than...
Did he sound like... One of the amazing things about Tatum is not just his speed and everything, but also his ear. Did he have that...?
